beats.subline: Tuesday, October 27, 2026 close — a chip-led rally as investors looked past Mideast oil jitters toward the Fed's rate decision and a heavy slate of tech earnings.
beats.body: Semiconductor names led the gains, with AMD, Marvell, Broadcom and Intel all jumping more than 3%, while energy stocks lagged as oil retreated; the advance came as the Fed opened a two-day policy meeting expected to end in a hold, with Microsoft and Alphabet earnings due after Wednesday's close.

beats.headline: UK charges two men over Iran-linked plot targeting air base used in US strikes on Iran
beats.body: Britain charged two men under its National Security Act over an alleged Iran-linked plot against RAF Fairford, the air base the US used to launch strikes on Iran, as Gulf-brokered mediation continued with Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials holding talks in Tehran that Iran called 'very good' but that produced no concrete breakthrough.

beats.headline: Taiwan accuses Beijing of orchestrating attack on comedian who satirized Xi; China dismisses claim
beats.body: Taiwan's government said China was behind last month's staged-car-accident attack on comedian Huang Yi-hao, whose act satirizes Xi Jinping, after prosecutors indicted five people accused of being paid to injure him; a Chinese Taiwan Affairs Office spokesperson dismissed the accusation as a fabrication by Taiwan's ruling party meant to stir anti-China sentiment ahead of elections.

beats.headline: CENTCOM estimates Iran war has cost the US military $47.1 billion so far
beats.body: A Central Command estimate obtained by CBS News puts the war's cost to the US military at roughly $47.1 billion as of mid-October, about $29 billion of it spent replacing expended munitions and excluding damage to US bases, even as a third carrier strike group has moved into the region and officials say the overall US force footprint is being quietly trimmed.

beats.headline: Anthropic strikes GSA deal cutting Claude prices 40% for US government agencies
beats.body: Anthropic expanded its partnership with the General Services Administration to give federal, state, local, tribal and territorial government buyers a 40% discount on Claude Enterprise, Claude for Government and the Claude API with no minimum spend commitment, a move Anthropic estimates will save government customers about $1 billion.

beats.headline: Bears' Monangai and Muhammad absent from Tuesday's practice ahead of Seahawks matchup
beats.body: Running back Kyle Monangai and cornerback Malik Muhammad were not seen for the open portion of Tuesday's practice, while linebackers D'Marco Jackson and TJ Edwards both returned to practice; Chicago's full Week 8 injury report isn't due until Thursday ahead of Monday night's game against Seattle.
